messages:
Jonas Kim: Heads up - were getting a spike of errors from /v1/embeddings around 14:07 UTC. Customers report 'invalid embedding dimension: expected 1024 got 1536' in responses. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/2387

Priya Menon: I see the same in Sentry and metrics. 400s up 40% and p95 latency for embeddings doubled since 14:05. Most traffic from customers 'docssearch' and 'marketpulse'.

DeployBot: Deployment 18b9f4b promoted to embeddings-prod at 14:03 UTC by auto-promote pipeline

Luis Ortega: 18b9f4b contained a model swap to redwood-emb-v3 (multispec). There was a last-minute registry tag change. Might be a wrong model variant with dim=1536. Pulling model manifest now.

Anika Singh: Can we short-circuit requests to embeddings to avoid churn? Suggest enabling circuit-breaker and route to fallback embeddings-v2 for known heavy customers.

Jonas Kim: Circuits up for heavy tails. Running: curl -X POST https://controlplane.prod/flags -d '{"embeddings_circuit": "on"}'

DeployBot: Circuit flag applied to embeddings-prod for orgs: docssearch, marketpulse

Luis Ortega: Model manifest snippet:
```
model_id: redwood-emb-v3-multi
variants:
 - id: v3-1024
   dim: 1024
 - id: v3-1536
   dim: 1536
active_variant: v3-1536
commit: 18b9f4b
```

Priya Menon: Ugh, active_variant is 1536. Why did registry choose that? The release notes said default should be 1024-compatible.

Anika Singh: Impact: some clients fall back to 400s, others get long tail latency as server tries to repack vectors. Support is fielding refunds requests. Tier-1 CS escalated to oncall.

Jonas Kim: Quick mitigation plan: 1) pin service to v3-1024, 2) disable auto-promote pipeline, 3) add alert rule for dimension-mismatch error token. I'll take 1 & 2.

Luis Ortega: Running pin command now:
```
redwoodctl deploy set-variant embeddings-prod redwood-emb-v3-multi:v3-1024 --force --reason "hotfix - dimension mismatch"
```

DeployBot: Variant switch in progress. Rolling restart of embeddings-server pods (4 replicas)

SupportBot: Note: capture request_id from failing responses. Use header X-Request-Id to correlate. Also collect model-version header for postmortem.

Priya Menon: Health check post-restart shows model.dim=1024 and 200 OK. Error rate dropping but still noisy because some clients cached older model-version headers.

Anika Singh: How did auto-promote pick 1536? Is registry tag resolution unstable for multispec models? We need a pre-deploy compatibility check to assert expected dimension matches service config.

Luis Ortega: Observed behavior: registry returns 'latest' which for multispec resolves to the highest-capacity variant by default. In this release, packaging team didn't mark v3-1536 as non-default. Pipeline assumes the default variant is backward-compatible.

Jonas Kim: Added immediate alert rule: if 'invalid embedding dimension' errors > 2% over 5m then page eng-oncall. Filed INF-558 for infra changes.

Priya Menon: Also noticed batching change in 18b9f4b that allows variable-dim batch packing which might have amplified errors when variant mismatched. Recommend disabling that feature until we validate variants.

Anika Singh: Can we add a deployment hook that checks /health.model.dimension matches expected dimension in config? If mismatch, abort. That should have prevented this.

Luis Ortega: Agreed. Opening infra PR: add model-dim preflight, and block auto-promote for multispec models unless explicitly approved. Link: https://infra.redwood.ai/INF-558

Jonas Kim: Customer comms: Priya please draft note explaining rollback and next steps. Offer 1 day of credit to affected orgs. Make sure to include steps for customers to detect dimension mismatch on their side (support playbook).

Priya Menon: Draft ready and sent to legal/comms. Support playbook repro steps:
- Call POST /v1/embeddings with sample inputs
- If response contains 'invalid embedding dimension' capture X-Request-Id and model-version header
- Query GET /health/model to check model.dimension and model.version
- If mismatch, ask customer to retry after 5 minutes and escalate with captured headers

Anika Singh: Post-incident tasks: 1) harden registry tagging rules, 2) add deployment dim-check, 3) add canary validation suite for embeddings (run few thousand sample requests across variants), 4) revert batching variable-dim pack if it causes repacking issues.

Luis Ortega: I'll own the registry/tagging fix. ETA: PR by EOD. Jonas can you own canary validation?

Jonas Kim: I'll take canary validation. Will add tests and integrate into auto-promote pipeline. ETA: 2 days.

DeployBot: Incident status: MITIGATED at 14:55 UTC. Metrics: 400s returned to baseline and latency back within SLO after rolling restart and circuit gating.

SupportBot: Runbook note appended: 'If multi-variant model introduced, validate active_variant.dim == expected_dim; if not, block promote and alert oncall.'

Priya Menon: Postmortem owner: Anika will lead with Luis & Jonas as co-authors. Deadline for draft: EOD next business day.

Anika Singh: Thanks team. Leaving thread open until postmortem published. If anyone sees residual customer reports, drop them here.
